# Draft:7th Armored Brigade during the Israel–Hamas war

During the Iron Swords War, the 7th Brigade fought in numerous battles. On October 7th, the first day of the war, the brigade played a significant role in repelling the Hamas terror attack. In the second phase of the fighting — the ground maneuver — brigade forces participated in operations deep within the Gaza Strip for a full year without interruption. Ahead of Operation Northern Arrows, the brigade moved north and took part in the ground maneuver in Lebanon during the Iron Swords War.
Background
On the morning of October 7, 2023 — a Saturday, Simchat Torah, 22nd of Tishrei 5784 — the terrorist organizations Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad launched the October 7 massacre. Under the cover of approximately 4,300 rocket launches, around 6,000 terrorists infiltrated from the Gaza Strip into dozens of Israeli communities, into Be’eri Forest, and into military installations in and around the Gaza envelope area. They entered through 119 breaches in the border fence, by air, and by sea, engaging in gun battles with outnumbered security forces.
The terrorists carried out massacres and acts of rape, murdered and killed 1,163 people — including 779 civilians — and abducted about 251 individuals to the Gaza Strip, among them men, women, the elderly, and infants.
In the first hours of the attack, emergency response teams, Israel Police officers, Yamam counterterrorism unit fighters, and IDF soldiers — despite being outnumbered — fought against the attackers. Around 1,609 terrorists were killed in Israeli territory during the battles. On the Israeli side, 329 soldiers, 58 police officers, and 10 members of the Israel Security Agency (Shin Bet) were killed.
Following the October 7 massacre, Israel declared the launch of the Iron Swords War with the goal of toppling Hamas rule in the Gaza Strip and eliminating all terrorists present there. At that time, Battalion 77 was stationed along the Gaza Strip front.
Here's a respectful and simple wording for a memorial sticker in Hebrew for Sgt. First Class (סמ"ר) Shai Levinson:
On the eve of the October 7 massacre, Battalion 77 served as the tank battalion of the Gaza Division (most of the tanks had been placed under the command of infantry battalions). The battalion headquarters was assigned responsibility for the northern sector of the brigade’s area. Within Battalion 77 was the Pechatak (the battalion’s Assault and Exposure Company), which took up position at the Erez outpost, while other forces were on guard duty and high alert at the Yiftach-Zikim outpost.
Meanwhile, Golani Brigade’s Battalion 13 and Battalion 51, along with the Nahal Reconnaissance Battalion, held the remaining stretch of the Gaza border line.
At the onset of the attack, the battalion’s tanks were dispatched toward pre-designated positions. Some of the tanks encountered anti-tank ambushes on their way and were forced to engage in combat while surrounded by terrorists on all sides.
The scale of the assault forced commanders to make extremely difficult decisions — choosing between defending civilian communities and protecting IDF outposts. These decisions often meant attempting to rescue civilians in towns and kibbutzim at the expense of military posts and soldiers.
The tanks fought with exceptional bravery, and some played a crucial role in preventing infiltrations or significantly hindering the terrorists' ability to enter communities. The crews fought as isolated units rather than in organized formations, and many sustained heavy casualties.
